words.gloss: that which will be lost and
that which will be produced and

literal: That which will be lost and, that which will be produced and, having become, afterwards will yield profit and, having considered, act.
translation: Weigh what will be lost, what will be gained, and the ultimate profit that will result, before undertaking an action.
modern: ஒரு செயலைத் தொடங்கும் முன், அதனால் அழியும் பொருளையும், ஆகும் பொருளையும், முடிவில் அது தரும் ஊதியத்தையும் ஆராய்ந்து செய்ய வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet advises careful calculation before starting any enterprise. The words 'aḻivatūum' and 'āvatūum' refer to the initial capital or effort expended and the immediate returns generated, both lengthened for musical emphasis. One must weigh these against the ultimate, long-term profit ('ūtiyam') that will result ('āki vaḻi payakkum'). Only after thoroughly considering all three factors should one proceed with the action.
